scope.description: Preserved read-only source findings and already observed inotify intervals. File opens can come from any process; they are progress observations, not CUDA, frame, packet or sanitizer completion. No target, monitor, GPU, SDK or tool-version changes were made for this investigation.

source_findings.finding: No frame-16 periodic branch was found in the inspected TrackingSession, FlowMotionCuda or tracking paths. This bounded source inspection is not a claim about private NVIDIA library internals.
FlowMotionCuda enqueue_estimate only uses the special first-frame branch frame!=0; it explicitly sets disableTemporalHints=NV_OF_TRUE for NvOFExecute.
The configured track bridge history capacity is 4, not 16.

Ordinary serial session work drains after each submitted frame. track_sequence opens the next JPEG before enqueueing it; the resulting open-to-open interval includes work and host overhead rather than attributing time to one kernel.
F04 adaptive sorting has data-dependent qualified-candidate branches at 100 and 512; launch shape stays fixed while shared-memory accesses can differ.
F04b batch sorting uses a small-batch path through 32 rows, with a radix path for larger batches.

Association work depends on predicted track and batch counts and executes four stages. These data-dependent paths are possible contributors to workload variation, not a diagnosis of the observed slowdown.

baseline_observation.method: Counted existing MOT output rows by one-based frame number; no dataset or GPU access.
baseline_observation.limitation: Emitted track row counts do not reveal pre-suppression qualified detections, suppressed rows or all association-state counts; they cannot rule out data-dependent workload changes.

preserved_input_open_observations.interpretation: The last two observed intervals decreased after the 230.29-second gap; the sampled series had not shown monotonic runaway through input21. This observation does not identify a cause or predict completion.

timeout_extension_assessment.description: GNU timeout has no documented live-duration extension command. Its SIGALRM handler marks timed_out and forwards the configured termination signal; SIGALRM is not a reset request. The independent service and root-controller deadlines would remain even if the timeout process were altered. Editing on-disk specs cannot change already running timers. Existing capture should remain unchanged; any later longer attempt must use a fresh capture with its actual timeout recorded.

sanitizer_complexity_boundary.description: NVIDIA documents that indirect barrier tracking can severely affect performance in some cases. This does not diagnose the active workload, establish a frame-16 mechanism or justify disabling checks.
